# Bakytzhan Kurmanbek: Python under the hood

Short lessons on what happens under the hood when everyday Python runs: the objects, the memory, the bytecode,
the data structures, drawn step by step. Each folder has the handout (PDF), a notebook you can run in seconds to
look inside on your own machine, and the code behind every picture.

| Lesson | What you'll see inside | Files |
|---|---|---|
| [How a Python dictionary finds a key](hash-lookup/) | What `ages["leo"]` does inside CPython 3.12.7: `hash()`, the slot its last bits pick, one entry, one compare; then the collision, the resize to 16 slots and why a list can't be a key, read out of a real dictionary's memory | [notes.pdf](hash-lookup/notes.pdf) · [notebook](hash-lookup/notebook.ipynb) · [code](hash-lookup/code/) |
| [How a database index finds a row: inside SQLite’s B-tree pages](db-index/) | What SQLite reads for one `WHERE email = ?`: the real pages, decoded from the database file, down the index's B-tree and the table's (1,000,000 rows, SQLite 3.45.3) | [notes.pdf](db-index/notes.pdf) · [notebook](db-index/notebook.ipynb) · [code](db-index/code/) |
| [What a Python list really holds: inside CPython’s list object](list-append/) | What `nums.append(7)` does inside a list: the slots read from memory and matched to `id()`, the spare room `sys.getsizeof` shows, a full block swapped for a bigger one, and the growth rule checked on 1,000 real appends (CPython 3.12.7) | [notes.pdf](list-append/notes.pdf) · [notebook](list-append/notebook.ipynb) · [code](list-append/code/) |
